correctness.rationale: The proof exhausts \(\omega(N)=1\) and \(\omega(N)=2\). The one-block case is equivalent to \((M-1)(p^a-1)=2\). In the two-block case, with \(A=p^a=x+1\), \(B=q^b=y+1\), and \(k=M-1\), the equation is exactly \(kxy=x+y+2\). A block \(A=2\) forces an impossible even divisor of \(3\); otherwise \(x,y\ge2\), the strict inequality \(2xy>x+y+2\) forces \(k=1\), and \((x-1)(y-1)=3\) gives \(\{A,B\}=\{3,5\}\). Direct substitution verifies \((2,3),(3,2),(15,2)\).
